q1.q: I'm reading a text that I find really difficult to understand. How can Mr.🆖 ProReader help me?
q1.a:
Mr.🆖 ProReader is built exactly for moments like that. Just upload your text (or snap a photo of it), and the AI goes to work in several ways:

  1. Before You Read — Prepare before you dive in: activate what you already know, learn the cultural background and key words, then skim the title, headings, and first/last paragraphs to predict what the text is about. After reading, check how close your prediction was.
  2. Instant Summary & Mind Map — Get a clear TL;DR, key points, and a visual mind map so you grasp the big picture before diving into the details.
  3. AI Text Visualization — The AI generates a vivid, colorful image that brings the main ideas to life! It automatically picks the best style — infographic, comic strip, cartoon, or painting — based on the text's genre. Available in English and Chinese.
  4. Simplified & Adapted Text — The app rewrites the passage at your level using simpler vocabulary and shorter sentences, while keeping the original meaning intact.
  5. Vocabulary Glossary — Every tricky word is highlighted and explained with bilingual definitions, syllable breakdowns, and example sentences. You can review them later with flashcards, spelling games, and quizzes powered by spaced repetition.
  6. Grammar Analysis — Complex grammar structures are identified and explained with patterns and examples from the text itself, plus interactive grammar games to reinforce your understanding.
  7. AI Tutor — A conversational AI tutor is always on standby. Ask it anything about the passage — highlight a confusing sentence, and it will break it down for you step by step.
  8. Reading Comprehension Test — Once you feel ready, take a generated quiz covering main ideas, details, inferences, and more, with detailed explanations for every answer.

Think of Mr.🆖 ProReader as a patient, personalized tutor that turns any difficult text into a learnable experience.

q2.q: If there's a word or phrase I don't understand in the text, what can I do?
q2.a:
You have two great options, each designed for a different learning moment:

Option 1: Highlight the word, add it, then tap to see its Glossary entry. Select any word or phrase in the text and tap "+ Add Word" on the toolbar. The word gets highlighted in yellow throughout the text. Once the AI has generated the Glossary, any highlighted words with a glossary entry will show a small amber dot. Tap the highlighted word and a popover appears with its bilingual definition, syllable breakdown, part of speech, and an example sentence. Every word you add is automatically saved to your personal vocabulary bank (My Vocabulary) for later review.

Option 2: Highlight the word and ask the AI Tutor. Select the word or phrase, then switch to the AI Tutor chat. The tutor already knows your text, so it will give you a deeper, more conversational explanation — not just a dictionary definition, but why that word is used in context, nuances like tone or connotation, and you can ask follow-up questions.

Glossary (Add Word → Tap)AI Tutor (Highlight → Ask)
SpeedInstant pop-up after glossary is generatedTakes a moment for AI to respond

InteractivityOne-way info displayTwo-way conversation — ask follow-ups

Pro tip: Combine both — use Option 1 to build your vocabulary list as you read, and turn to the AI Tutor whenever you need a deeper explanation. The words you save through Option 1 are the ones that get reinforced later through flashcards, spelling games, and quizzes with spaced repetition.

q3.q: I know most of the words in a sentence, but I still don't understand what the sentence is saying. What can I do?
q3.a:
That's a really common experience — understanding individual words but missing the meaning of the whole sentence is usually about sentence structure, grammar, or idiomatic usage. Mr.🆖 ProReader has three powerful tools to help:

1. Sentence Analysis — Select (highlight) the confusing sentence and tap the brain icon on the selection toolbar. The AI produces a detailed breakdown: sentence summary, vocabulary analysis, syntactic analysis (sentence type, clause structure, tricky grammar), pragmatic analysis (function in context, figures of speech, tone), and practical learning tips. The analyzed sentence gets underlined in blue so you can revisit it anytime.

2. AI Tutor — Highlight the sentence and take it to the AI Tutor chat. The tutor explains the sentence in context — not just what it means, but how it fits into the paragraph and why the author phrased it that way. You can ask follow-up questions like "Can you rephrase this in simpler words?" or "What does 'X' refer to?"

3. Grammar Analysis — If confusing sentences keep popping up, it might be a grammar pattern you haven't mastered yet. Run Grammar Analysis to scan for topics (tenses, conditionals, passive voice, etc.) with explanations and examples from your text. Reinforce your understanding with Grammar Games like Word Scramble, Error Surgery, and Grammar Roulette.

Pro tip: Start with Sentence Analysis for a quick, structured breakdown. If the sentence is part of a bigger confusion, bring it to the AI Tutor. And if you notice a pattern — like always struggling with passive voice — head to Grammar Analysis to tackle the root cause.

q4.q: Vocabulary building is key to improving my reading, but it's really difficult and boring to remember so many new words. What can I do?
q4.a:
We totally get it — rote memorization is a drag. That's why Mr.🆖 ProReader turns vocabulary building into something that feels less like studying and more like playing:

1. Vocabulary comes to you naturally — As you read, simply highlight and add unfamiliar words. The AI automatically generates bilingual definitions, syllable breakdowns, and example sentences. No manual data entry needed.

2. Flashcards with Spaced Repetition — The built-in flashcard system uses a scientifically-backed Leitner 5-box algorithm. Rate each card with Again, Hard, Good, or Easy, and it schedules the next review accordingly (1 day to 30 days). Over time, you spend less time on easy words and more on the ones that need reinforcement.

3. Spelling Games — Four interactive modes make active recall feel like play: Listen & Type, Scramble, Fill in the Blanks, and Mixed. Choose difficulty levels, word count, and Time Challenge mode for extra adrenaline.

4. Vocabulary Quiz — Auto-generated quizzes from your own word list with difficulty levels and Time Challenge mode.

5. My Vocabulary page — A personal word command center with sortable table, flashcards, spelling games, quizzes, auto-select strategies (overdue, hard, random, new, oldest), named review lists, export to PDF/Word/CSV, and review history.

6. Shared by your teacher — Teachers can share vocabulary lists and review lists directly with you. Accept a shared list and the words are added to your vocabulary bank automatically.

Pro tip: After each reading session, spend just 5–10 minutes on flashcards or a quick spelling game. The spaced repetition system shows you words right when you're about to forget them — the scientifically best time to reinforce memory. Small, consistent doses beat cramming every time.

q5.q: I often struggle with questions in school reading exams, especially DSE exam practices. How can Mr.🆖 ProReader help?
q5.a:
Mr.🆖 ProReader's Reading Comprehension Test simulates real exam conditions and targets the skills that DSE and school exams test:

1. Auto-generated, exam-style questions — Upload any text and the AI generates 10 questions tailored to your age and school level (Primary / Secondary / DSE). Question types mirror real exams: Multiple Choice, True/False/Not Given, Vocabulary in Context, Referencing, Inference, and Short Answer. For DSE students, the distribution is weighted heavily toward inference (3 questions) and vocabulary in context (2 questions).

2. Detailed explanations with skill tracking — Every question is tagged with the skill it tests: Main Idea, Detail, Inference, Vocabulary, or Author's Purpose. After submitting, you get a skill-by-skill breakdown and detailed explanations for every answer in both English and Chinese.

3. Retry missed questions and targeted practice — Retry Missed lets you re-attempt only the wrong ones. Targeted Practice generates a brand new set of questions focused specifically on your weakest skills.

Pro tip: After each reading session, generate a test and treat it like a real exam — don't look at the text while answering. Then use Targeted Practice to get fresh questions for your weakest skills. Repeat across different texts for steady improvement.

q6.q: I don't know what text to read. I just want to read more to practice for the DSE.
q6.a:
Mr.🆖 ProReader has you covered even before you start reading:

1. Text Repository — A built-in library of reading texts uploaded and shared by your teachers or school. Browse by visibility: Class (your specific class), School (everyone in your school), or Public (all schools). Pick a text, tap "Load," and you're ready to go.

2. "Pick a text for me" — Every time you open Mr.🆖 ProReader, a welcome dialog offers a "Read from Repository" option. The app randomly picks a text with a preview of the title and opening lines. Not feeling it? Hit "Pick another" until one catches your eye, then tap "Start Reading."

3. Upload your own DSE practice materials — Snap a photo (PNG, JPG, WEBP), upload a PDF, or paste text directly. The AI-powered OCR extracts the text, and all features become available.

4. AI Text Generator — Still can't find the right text? Open the AI Generate tab, type any topic or theme (e.g. "online safety", "a day at the beach"), choose a text type and length, and the AI writes a brand-new reading passage calibrated to your age and CEFR level. See Question 11 in the FAQ for details.

Pro tip: The app already comes with all DSE past exam papers from 2012 onwards pre-loaded in the Text Repository. Make it a habit: one past paper a day, work through it with the glossary and adapted text, then take the Reading Test. Consistent daily practice with real exam material is one of the most effective ways to prepare.

q7.q: I'm working on a DSE past paper and struggling with a very hard question. Can Mr.🆖 ProReader help me?
q7.a:
Absolutely! Here's how:

1. Upload the past paper — Upload it as a photo, PDF, or paste the text. The app extracts the text and generates a full suite of learning aids — summary, mind map, adapted text, glossary — so you have a solid understanding of the passage.

2. AI Tutor — your on-demand exam coach — Type or paste the exam question into the AI Tutor chat, and it guides you through how to approach it step by step. You can also highlight the relevant part of the text and ask how it connects to the question. The tutor uses Socratic questioning — guiding you to discover the answer through hints rather than just telling you.

3. Upload an image of the question — Snap a photo of the exam question and upload it directly in the AI Tutor chat. Three levels of help are available: "Hint me" (always available — guiding questions so you find the answer yourself), "Step-by-step" (requires Jailbreak Mode in Settings), and "Give Answer" (requires both Jailbreak Mode and Show 'Give Answer' in Settings).

Pro tip: Resist the urge to go straight to "Give Answer." Start with "Hint me" — the process of reasoning through it yourself is exactly what builds the skills you need on exam day. Use "Step-by-step" or "Give Answer" only when you're truly stuck.

q8.q: Can I come back to a text I read earlier, and on a different device?
q8.a:
Yes! Mr.🆖 ProReader automatically saves your reading sessions and syncs them to the cloud.

1. Automatic cloud saving — Every reading session is automatically saved to your account, including the full text, glossary, highlighted words, flashcard progress, reading test results, grammar analysis, tutor chat history, and all other work. There's no "Save" button — it just happens.

2. Resume from any device — Sign in with the same Google account on any device. Tap the bar chart icon in the header to open "Learning Journey," switch to the "Sessions" tab (clock icon), and all your past reading sessions are listed there. Tap any session to reload it exactly as you left it. Your settings and preferences also sync across devices.

3. Session management — From the Sessions tab, you can load a previous session to continue, export for backup, delete sessions, or share with others.

Pro tip: Start reading on your phone during a commute, then pick up the same text on your laptop at home. Everything — tutor chat, vocabulary progress, test scores — travels with you. Just make sure you're signed in with the same Google account on all devices.

q9.q: Can I track and see my learning progress and history?
q9.a:
Yes! Mr.🆖 ProReader makes it easy to see the big picture and dive into the details:

1. Learning Journey — Tap the bar chart icon in the header to open "Learning Journey." The Overview tab shows cumulative stats: total reading texts, summaries, mind maps, adapted texts, sentences analyzed, vocabulary collected, AI Tutor questions, and average learning progress, plus score trends and AI feature usage breakdown. The Sessions tab lists all past reading sessions with details.

2. Achievements — Automatically earn achievement badges across 12 different types — from reading sessions to vocabulary quizzes. Each badge tracks milestones and motivates you to keep going.

3. Leaderboard — Compare your reading activity, test scores, and vocabulary growth with classmates or other students.

4. My Vocabulary — See every word you've ever encountered with mastery levels (0–5), review counts, accuracy rates, and SRS scheduling status.

Pro tip: Check the Overview tab in Learning Journey once a week. Seeing your stats grow over time is a powerful motivator. If you notice your Reading Test scores plateauing on a particular skill, that's your signal to focus targeted practice on that area.

q10.q: I'm a teacher / school administrator. What additional features are available for me?
q10.a:
Mr.🆖 ProReader has a full set of management and monitoring tools for teachers and administrators:

For Teachers:

  • Teacher Dashboard — Real-time class analytics: daily learning activity, AI features usage, score tracking (Reading Test, Spelling, Quiz, Grammar). Filter by class and time period.
  • Student Data — Detailed reading session data per student. Filter by class and date range. Export to Excel for record-keeping.
  • AI Questions Tracker — Track every question students ask the AI Tutor, including frequency and which students asked.
  • Text Repository — Upload reading materials with visibility control (class-only, school, or public). Edit, rename, delete, import/export.
  • Share vocabulary & review lists — Share curated vocabulary and named review lists directly with students.
  • Manage classes — Create classes, assign students, edit class details.

For Administrators — everything above, plus:

  • User Management — Manage users within your school and assign teacher/student roles.
  • School Subscriptions — Purchase and manage subscriptions for your entire school with seat allocation.

Pro tip: Use the AI Questions Tracker to discover common misconceptions. If multiple students ask about the same concept, address it in your next lesson. Combined with Student Data and Excel exports, you have everything you need for data-driven teaching.

q11.q: I want to practice reading but I don't have a text. Can Mr.🆖 ProReader generate one for me?
q11.a:
Yes! The AI Text Generator writes a brand-new reading passage from scratch, tailored to your level. Open the AI Generate tab (next to Upload and Text Repository) and:

  1. Enter a topic or theme — Anything you're curious about: "space exploration", "online safety", "a day at the beach". Add an optional description for more direction (e.g. "the main character is a shy 14-year-old").
  2. Pick a text type — Article, report, blog post, review, email/letter, editorial/argumentative essay, interview, short story, advertisement/brochure, notice/announcement, or profile/feature.
  3. Choose a length — From ~250 to ~1150 words.
  4. Set the difficulty — A CEFR level (A1–C2) is auto-suggested from your age; adjust it up or down for stronger or weaker students.

The AI follows explicit vocabulary and grammar rules for your CEFR band, self-checks the word count and Flesch-Kincaid grade level, and returns the text plus a quality-control summary (estimated grade, new vocabulary). Once generated, every reading tool unlocks — summary, glossary, mind map, reading test, grammar analysis, and more. Not quite right? Tap Easier or Harder to regenerate at one CEFR band up or down.

Pro tip: Match the text type to the skill you're practicing. Working on argumentative writing for DSE? Generate an "editorial / argumentative essay". Practicing everyday reading? Try a "blog post" or "notice / announcement". The generated text is a fresh starting point — run the Reading Test on it for a complete practice cycle.

q12.q: Can I challenge my classmates to a live spelling battle?
q12.a:
Yes! The Multiplayer Spelling Battle supports multiple game modes (Listen & Type, Letter Scramble, Fill Blanks, or Mixed) in a real-time competition.

For Students: Open Spelling Challenge → click Multiplayer Battle. Create a room (pick your game mode and word source) or join one with a 6-character code. The host starts the game — a 3-2-1 countdown begins, then each word challenge adapts to your chosen mode. A live ranking shows everyone's score after every word. At the end you see the final ranking, your tier badge, and accuracy. Results count toward your spelling best score, the leaderboard, and SRS mastery — just like solo play.

For Teachers: Create or join rooms like any student. Additionally, toggle Class Battle when creating a room and pick a target class — all students in that class receive a notification (persistent toast + red badge on the header bell) with the room code. They can join from anywhere in the app, not just the spelling page.

q12.q: Can I challenge my classmates to a live spelling battle?
q12.a:
Yes! The Multiplayer Spelling Battle supports multiple game modes (Listen & Type, Letter Scramble, Fill Blanks, or Mixed) in a real-time competition.

For Students: Open Spelling Challenge → click Multiplayer Battle. Create a room (pick your game mode and word source) or join one with a 6-character code. The host starts the game — a 3-2-1 countdown begins, then each word challenge adapts to your chosen mode. A live ranking shows everyone's score after every word. At the end you see the final ranking, your tier badge, and accuracy. Results count toward your spelling best score, the leaderboard, and SRS mastery — just like solo play.

For Teachers: Create or join rooms like any student. Additionally, toggle Class Battle when creating a room and pick a target class — all students in that class receive a notification (persistent toast + red badge on the header bell) with the room code. They can join from anywhere in the app, not just the spelling page.

Tip: Host can start a rematch after the game ends. Up to 35 players per room.

If I haven't selected anything, don't pick a word yourself; instead ask me to select a word or phrase first. Otherwise, explain it in a few warm, clear sentences and weave in all of the following: what it means, in simple student-friendly English; a Traditional Chinese (繁體中文) meaning; its part of speech (noun, verb, adjective, etc., or say 'phrase' if it's a multi-word expression like a phrasal verb or idiom); and a short example sentence using it in context. If it's a single word, also tell me how to say it by breaking it into syllables with the stressed syllable in CAPITALS (e.g. ex·AM·ple); if it's a phrase, skip the syllable breakdown. overview.intro: My Vocabulary collects every glossary word from your reading sessions into one place for systematic review. Words are automatically synced — just read and they appear here.

due.desc: Words whose next review time has passed. Shown in orange — review these soon!

mastered.name: Mastered
mastered.desc: Words that reached the highest mastery level (Level 5) through repeated correct reviews.

new.name: New Words
new.desc: Words you haven't reviewed yet. Start reviewing to track your progress!

table.title: Word Table
table.desc: Browse, search, sort, and filter all your words. Select words manually or use Auto Select, then start a review.

studyPlan.name: Study Plan
studyPlan.desc: A quick-start dialog that opens when you arrive. Pick a preset (due, new, hard, or random words), choose a review mode, and begin in two taps. Dismiss it to browse manually.

clickableStats.name: Tap to Filter

review.intro: Choose from three review modes. Select words or phrases first (or accept a shared review list), then pick a mode.

flashcard.name: Flashcard
flashcard.desc: Flip cards to reveal definitions, then rate your confidence with SRS buttons:

again.name: Again
again.desc: Shows the word again almost immediately. Marks it as Hard.

hard.name: Hard
hard.desc: Re-inserts the word in the middle of the queue. Marks it as Hard.

good.name: Good
good.desc: Moves the word to the end of the queue. Counts as correct.

easy.name: Easy
easy.desc: Removes the word from the queue. Marks it as Easy.

quiz.name: Quiz
quiz.desc: Multiple-choice questions testing word meanings. Great for quick self-checks.

spelling.name: Spelling
spelling.desc: Type the correct spelling of each word. Perfect for memorizing word forms.

srs.title: Spaced Repetition (SRS)
srs.desc: Words move through 6 levels (New → L1 → L2 → L3 → L4 → Mastered). Correct answers advance a level; incorrect answers drop back. Higher levels have longer review intervals (1 day → 3 days → 7 days → 14 days → 30 days).

extras.intro: Additional tools to help you manage and share your vocabulary.

autoSelect.name: Auto Select
autoSelect.desc: Automatically pick words based on a strategy. Choose how many words to select, then pick the strategy that fits your goal.

due.name: Due for Review
due.desc: Words whose scheduled review time has arrived — the most overdue appear first. Your daily SRS checklist.

hardest.name: Hardest Words
hardest.desc: Words you labelled "Hard" with the SRS buttons, starting from the lowest mastery level. Tackle stubborn words you struggle with.

newest.name: Newest Words
newest.desc: Words you've never reviewed, most recently added first. Ideal for learning fresh vocabulary.

random.name: Random Mix
random.desc: All your words shuffled at random. Great for a varied, balanced study session.

weakest.name: Weakest Words
weakest.desc: Lowest accuracy in past reviews — the words you get wrong most often. Ranked by fewest correct answers per attempt.

export.name: Export
export.desc: Download your words as Glossary (PDF), Flashcard Sheets, Fill-in-the-Blank, or Matching Exercise worksheets.

reviewLists.name: Review Lists

share.name: Share Vocabulary
share.desc: Teachers can share selected words directly with students. Shared words are labelled "Teacher" in the student's table.

history.name: Review History
history.desc: See past review sessions with per-word results. Flashcard sessions show Again/Hard/Good/Easy counts; Quiz and Spelling sessions show accuracy.

tip.title: Tip
tip.content: Use Auto Select with "Due for Review" to quickly catch up on overdue words, or "Random Mix" for a balanced study session.

overview.intro: The Overview tab provides visual analytics of your reading and learning activity, including stat cards, activity charts, score distributions, and vocabulary growth over time.

statCards.name: Summary Stat Cards
statCards.desc: Three cards at the top show your total Reading Texts (with upload/repository breakdown), Total Vocabulary size, and Average Learning Progress across all sessions.

dailyActivity.name: Daily Learning Activity
dailyActivity.desc: A stacked bar chart showing your daily learning activities across 17 types including reading, pre-reading summaries, mind maps, text visualizations, glossary, collocations, flashcard reviews, tests, quizzes, spelling and grammar games, and AI Tutor questions. Use the time range buttons to adjust the window.

readingActivity.name: Reading Activity
readingActivity.desc: An area chart showing how many reading sessions you completed each week. The x-axis shows week ranges so you can track consistency over time.

aiFeatures.name: AI Features Usage
aiFeatures.desc: A horizontal bar chart breaking down your usage of 11 AI-powered features: pre-reading summaries, mind maps (English and Chinese shown as stacked segments), text visualizations, adapted texts, simplified texts, sentence analysis, glossary, phrases & collocations, grammar analysis, and AI Tutor questions.

readingTestDist.name: Reading Test Score Distribution
readingTestDist.desc: A bar chart showing how your reading test scores are distributed across four score buckets: 0–25%, 26–50%, 51–75%, and 76–100%.

vocabQuizDist.name: Vocab Quiz Score Distribution
vocabQuizDist.desc: A bar chart showing how your vocabulary quiz scores are distributed across four performance buckets.

spellingTrend.name: Spelling Score Trend
spellingTrend.desc: A line chart tracking your spelling scores across sessions. Watch your scores improve over time.

spellingAccuracy.name: Spelling Accuracy
spellingAccuracy.desc: A line chart tracking your spelling accuracy percentage across sessions. Shows your precision in spelling challenges.

grammarQuizDist.name: Grammar Quiz Score Distribution
grammarQuizDist.desc: A bar chart showing how your grammar quiz scores are distributed across four performance buckets.

grammarGameTrend.name: Grammar Game Score Trend
grammarGameTrend.desc: A line chart tracking your grammar game scores across sessions. See how your grammar skills develop over time.

grammarGameAccuracy.name: Grammar Game Accuracy
grammarGameAccuracy.desc: A line chart tracking your grammar game accuracy percentage across sessions. Shows your precision in grammar challenges.

vocabularyGrowth.name: Vocabulary Growth
vocabularyGrowth.desc: An area chart tracking your cumulative vocabulary growth over time. Choose from 13 time ranges (1W to 3Y) to view your vocabulary accumulation over different periods.

skillProfile.name: Reading Comprehension Skill Profile
skillProfile.desc: A radar chart showing your accuracy across 5 reading comprehension skills (Main Idea, Detail, Inference, Vocabulary, Purpose), aggregated from every completed reading test. The caption highlights your weakest skill so you can focus your practice.

tip.title: Pro Tip:
tip.content: Focus on consistency! Regular daily activity builds stronger learning habits than occasional bursts. Use the time range selectors to track your weekly and monthly progress.

timeRange.name: Time Range Selectors
timeRange.desc: Charts with time-dependent data offer range buttons (7d to 360d for daily activity, 1W to 3Y for vocabulary growth). Click any range to focus on a specific period.

scoreBuckets.name: Score Distribution Buckets
scoreBuckets.desc: Score distribution charts group your scores into four color-coded buckets: red (0–25%), orange (26–50%), green (51–75%), blue (76–100%).

tooltips.name: Interactive Tooltips
tooltips.desc: Hover over any bar, line, or data point to see detailed breakdowns including exact values, activity counts, and score details.

sessions.intro: The Sessions tab lets you browse, search, import, assign, share, and manage all your reading sessions in a detailed table view.

importSessions.name: Import Sessions
importSessions.desc: Upload JSON session files to restore previously exported reading sessions. Accepts .json files exported from the app.

search.name: Search Sessions
search.desc: Fuzzy-search across your sessions by reading text content and summaries. Quickly find specific sessions from your history.

sessionTable.name: Session Table
sessionTable.desc: A detailed table showing each session's reading text title, learning progress %, vocabulary count, spelling score, quiz score, test score, grammar quiz score, grammar game score, accuracy, and last update date.

assignHomework.name: Assign as Homework
assignHomework.desc: Turn a reading session into a trackable class assignment. Opens a dialog to set a title, subject, due date, and select students to distribute the homework to.

shareSession.name: Share Session
shareSession.desc: Share a reading session with classmates or students. Opens a dialog to select recipients grouped by class and school.

tip.title: Pro Tip:

charts.intro: The dashboard provides 14 visual charts to help you monitor student progress, identify learning gaps, and track engagement at a glance.

dailyActivity.name: Daily Learning Activity
dailyActivity.desc: A stacked bar chart showing each student's learning activities for a specific date. Navigate between dates to see daily breakdowns across 17 activity types.

readingTexts.name: Reading Texts
readingTexts.desc: A bar chart showing how many reading texts each student has worked on. Use time-period filters (1W to 1Y) to focus on recent activity. Bars are color-coded by quartile.

totalVocabulary.name: Total Vocabulary
totalVocabulary.desc: A bar chart displaying each student's total vocabulary size. The dashed reference line shows the class average for quick comparison.

avgProgress.name: Avg Learning Progress
avgProgress.desc: A bar chart showing each student's average learning progress (0–100%). Use this to identify students who may need additional support.

aiFeatures.name: AI Features Usage
aiFeatures.desc: A stacked bar chart breaking down how each student uses 11 AI-powered features: pre-reading summaries, mind maps, visualizations, adapted texts, simplified texts, sentence analysis, glossary, phrases & collocations, grammar, and AI Tutor.

readingTestDist.name: Reading Test Score Distribution
readingTestDist.desc: A stacked bar chart showing how each student's reading test scores are distributed across four score buckets: 0–25%, 26–50%, 51–75%, and 76–100%.

vocabQuizDist.name: Vocabulary Quiz Score Distribution
vocabQuizDist.desc: A stacked bar chart showing each student's vocabulary quiz scores grouped into four performance buckets. Helps identify mastery levels across the class.

grammarQuizDist.name: Grammar Quiz Score Distribution
grammarQuizDist.desc: A stacked bar chart showing each student's grammar quiz scores grouped into four performance buckets. Useful for spotting grammar understanding gaps.

grammarGameScore.name: Grammar Game Score
grammarGameScore.desc: A bar chart displaying each student's average grammar game score. The dashed line shows the class average.

grammarGameAccuracy.name: Grammar Game Accuracy Distribution
grammarGameAccuracy.desc: A stacked bar chart showing each student's grammar game accuracy across four buckets. Helps identify which students have strong grammar fundamentals.

spellingScore.name: Spelling Score
spellingScore.desc: A bar chart displaying each student's average spelling score. Useful for tracking spelling proficiency across the class.

spellingAccuracy.name: Spelling Accuracy
spellingAccuracy.desc: A bar chart displaying each student's average spelling accuracy. The dashed line shows the class average. Helps identify students who struggle with spelling.

vocabularyGrowth.name: Vocabulary Growth
vocabularyGrowth.desc: A multi-line area chart tracking cumulative vocabulary growth over time for each student. Choose from 13 time ranges (1W to 3Y) and toggle individual students on/off.

skillAverages.name: Class Reading Comprehension Skill Profile
skillAverages.desc: A radar chart showing the class's average accuracy across 5 reading comprehension skills (Main Idea, Detail, Inference, Vocabulary, Purpose), aggregated from every completed reading test. The caption highlights the class's weakest skill so you can target instruction.

tip.title: Pro Tip:
tip.content: Use the Excel export to capture all 14 charts with detailed student data for offline analysis, parent meetings, or progress reports.

studentToggle.desc: In the Vocabulary Growth chart, click on student names in the legend to show or hide their data lines. Focus on specific students or compare groups.

quartileColors.desc: Bar charts use a four-color system: Q1 (red, 0–25%), Q2 (orange, 25–50%), Q3 (green, 50–75%), Q4 (blue, 75–100%). Students are ranked and colored by their position.

scoreBuckets.name: Score Distribution Buckets
scoreBuckets.desc: Score distribution charts group individual scores into four color-coded buckets: red (0–25%), orange (26–50%), green (51–75%), blue (76–100%).

referenceLines.name: Class Average Reference Line
referenceLines.desc: A dashed reference line on charts shows the class average, making it easy to identify students who are above or below average at a glance.

tooltips.name: Interactive Tooltips
tooltips.desc: Hover over any bar or data point to see detailed breakdowns including exact values, activity counts, and score distributions for individual students.

excelExport.name: Export to Excel
excelExport.desc: Generate a comprehensive Excel report with all 14 charts as images plus 3 data sheets: Student Overview, AI Features breakdown, and Score Details with conditional formatting.

tabsContent.intro: The User Management panel provides six tabs for managing schools, users, classes, student data, AI questions, and subscriptions. Available tabs depend on your role.

schools.name: Schools
schools.desc: View, edit, and delete schools. Each school has a name and email domain. Deleting a school un-assigns all its users. Super-admin only.

users.name: Users
users.desc: View all users in a sortable, filterable table. Change roles (student, teacher, admin), assign users to schools, and assign students to classes. Filter by role, class, or school.

classes.name: Classes
classes.desc: Create, edit, and delete classes. Assign a teacher to each class and manage student membership. Teachers see only their own classes.

classMembers.name: Class Members
classMembers.desc: Opened from the Classes tab. View all students in a class, add new students from the same school, or remove existing members. Search available students by name.

studentData.name: Student Data
studentData.desc: View detailed reading session data for students across classes. Filter by school, class, date range, or search by student name. Export filtered data to Excel for offline analysis.

aiQuestions.name: AI Questions
aiQuestions.desc: View aggregated AI Tutor questions asked by students. See question frequency, unique user counts, and last-asked dates. Click any question to expand and view individual instances with AI responses.

subscriptions.name: Subscriptions
subscriptions.desc: Manage individual and school subscription plans. View active, canceled, and trial subscriptions. Admin and super-admin only.

tip.title: Pro Tip:
tip.content: Use the class filter dropdowns across tabs to quickly narrow your view to a specific group of students. The Student Data tab remembers your class selection.

featuresContent.intro: Common interactive features available across tabs to help you find, organize, and manage data efficiently.

sorting.name: Sorting
sorting.desc: Click any column header to sort the table by that column. Click again to reverse the sort direction. Sorted tables remember your preference while browsing.

filtering.name: Filtering
filtering.desc: Use dropdown filters to narrow results by role, class, or school. Filters work together — combine role and class filters to find specific groups of users.

pagination.name: Pagination
pagination.desc: All tables display 20 items per page with page navigation at the bottom. Large datasets are split across pages for faster loading.

roleManagement.name: Role Management
roleManagement.desc: Change user roles inline using the role dropdown in the Users tab. Super-admins can assign any role; admins can assign teacher and student roles.

schoolAssignment.name: School Assignment
schoolAssignment.desc: Assign users to schools using the school dropdown in the Users tab. Only available to super-admins. Students must have a school before being assigned to a class.

bulkActions.name: Bulk Actions
bulkActions.desc: Select multiple users with checkboxes in the Users tab, then use the bulk action button to revoke school access for all selected users at once.

search.name: Search
search.desc: Search across Student Data by student name, email, or reading text title. In AI Questions, search by question text. Results update as you type.

dateRange.name: Date Range Filter
dateRange.desc: In Student Data and AI Questions tabs, filter by time period: 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, 180 days, 360 days, or all time. Focus on recent activity or view the full history.

exportImport.name: Export / Import Backup
exportImport.desc: Super-admins can export a full system backup (.zip) including all users, classes, and reading sessions with images. Import a backup to merge data into the system.

testEmails.name: Test Emails
testEmails.desc: Super-admins can send test emails for 9 different email templates (reminders, subscription notifications, etc.) to verify email delivery is working correctly.

excelExport.name: Excel Export
excelExport.desc: In the Student Data tab, export the currently filtered session data to an Excel file with formatted columns for offline analysis or reporting.

studentDataDetails.name: Click-to-View Details
studentDataDetails.desc: In the Student Data tab, click any value in the Reading Text, Vocabulary Count, Vocabulary Quiz, Grammar Quiz, or Reading Test columns to view full details in a popup dialog — including the original text with vocabulary highlights, glossary table, quiz questions with the student's answers (color-coded green/red), and adapted/simplified text tabs.

tip.title: Pro Tip:
tip.content: Use Export before making bulk changes to create a safety net. The import feature merges data, so you can restore specific records without overwriting everything.

overview.intro: The Assignments page lists every reading task your teacher has shared with you, or that you have assigned to your students.

list.name: Assignment cards
list.desc: Each card shows the title, subject, description, status, due date and progress at a glance.

status.name: Status badges
status.desc: Active assignments are in progress; archived ones are hidden from students but kept for reference.

due.name: Due dates
due.desc: When a due date passes and progress is below 100%, an Overdue badge highlights what needs attention.

detail.name: Open details
detail.desc: Click any assignment title to open its detail page with the full roster, scores and per-student progress.

tracking.intro: Track how students are doing at a glance and spot assignments that need follow-up.

avgProgress.name: Average progress
avgProgress.desc: The TrendingUp icon shows the average completion across all assigned students for each assignment.

studentCount.desc: See how many students are included in each assignment at a glance.

overdue.name: Overdue alerts
overdue.desc: Past-due assignments with incomplete work are flagged in red so you can follow up quickly.

roster.name: Per-student breakdown
roster.desc: Open an assignment to view test scores, vocabulary, spelling, grammar scores and the last-viewed time for each student.

srs.title: Tip:
srs.desc: Sort any column on the detail page by clicking its header to find students who need help fastest.

manage.intro: Teachers and admins can create, edit and track assignments from this page.

gettingStarted.title: Getting started
gettingStarted.step1: Click the "Create assignment" button in the top-right corner.
gettingStarted.step2: In the dialog that opens, find the reading session you want to assign.
gettingStarted.step3: Click the graduation-cap icon next to that session to select it.
gettingStarted.step4: Pick your students (or load a saved roster), then optionally set a title, subject, due date and instructions.
gettingStarted.step5: Click "Create assignment (N)" to confirm — students will see it on their Assignments page immediately.

create.name: Create assignment
create.desc: Click "Create assignment", pick a reading session with the graduation-cap icon, select students and optionally set a due date.

presets.name: Class presets
presets.desc: Save reusable groups of students as rosters so you can assign work to the same class in one click next time.

edit.name: Edit, archive, delete
edit.desc: Use the actions at the bottom of each card to update details, archive when done, or permanently delete an assignment.

export.name: Export to Excel
export.desc: On the detail page, export the full roster with scores and progress to an Excel file for grading or records.

tip.title: Note:
tip.content: Archiving hides an assignment from students without deleting their work — useful at the end of a term.
